papers.title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
papers.abstract: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ > G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦矿化脱细胞基质-海藻酸生物墨水的材料配方与骨缺损修复，未涉及任何AI或打印过程智能决策，仅与生物打印材料背景相关。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML component is integrated into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is a materials-formulation and ex vivo study without data-driven modeling, print-process monitoring, or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有生物墨水难以在骨缺损处提供初始承载支撑。
summary_zh.method: 以山羊脱细胞基质为模板矿化生成羟基磷灰石，并与海藻酸共混制备可打印生物墨水。
summary_zh.result: 矿化墨水力学强度提升，细胞活性和成骨分化增强，离体缺损模型中即刻提供结构支撑。
summary_zh.validation: 流变、力学测试、细胞实验及山羊离体骨缺损模型验证。

summary_en.motivation: Current bioinks lack the mechanical capacity to bear initial load at critical-sized bone defects.
summary_en.method: Goat-derived decellularized matrix was used as a mineralization template to nucleate hydroxyapatite, then blended with alginate into a printable bioink.
summary_en.result: The mineralized ink improved compressive strength, osteoblast viability, and osteogenic differentiation, and provided immediate structural reinforcement in an ex vivo defect model.
summary_en.validation: Rheological and mechanical characterization, in vitro osteoblast culture, and a caprine ex vivo bone defect model.

papers.title: Influence of stem undersizing during direct anterior approach for total hip arthroplasty on periprosthetic bone biomechanics: a finite element analysis
papers.abstract: Aims Stem undersizing during cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) may occur more frequently when the procedure is performed through the direct anterior approach (DAA) because of limited femoral exposure. Insufficient stem–bone contact may compromise primary stability and alter load transfer in the proximal femur. The aim was to investigate the biomechanical effects of femoral stem undersizing on periprosthetic bone using finite element analysis. A secondary objective was to evaluate whether the presence of a femoral stem collar modifies these biomechanical effects. Methods Patient-specific finite element models of the full femur were generated from CT data. Eight finite element models were analyzed, combining four implantation configurations of the AMIStem-P designs (Adequate Fit, Adequate Fit–Collared, Undersized, and Undersized–Collared) with two cancellous bone density conditions, representing 100% and 90% cancellous bone density. A hip joint force representing the peak loading phase during normal walking/single-leg support was applied. Strain intensity in periprosthetic trabecular bone was assessed according to Frost’s mechanostat theory, and von Mises stress distribution in the femoral stem was evaluated. Results Stem undersizing markedly increased strain intensity in the periprosthetic trabecular bone and enlarged regions exceeding the mechanostat overload threshold (> 3,000 µε). Adequate stem–bone fit with cortical support substantially reduced the volume of overloaded bone tissue. The presence of a collar reduced strain levels, particularly in undersized configurations, indicating improved proximal load transfer. Reduced cancellous bone density resulted in a moderate additional increase in strain. Simulated load reduction markedly decreased periprosthetic strain levels. Implant stresses remained well below material limits. Conclusion Femoral stem undersizing may substantially increase strain within the periprosthetic trabecular bone and enlarge regions exposed to overload conditions. Achieving adequate stem–bone fit with cortical support was associated with a marked reduction in periprosthetic bone strain. The presence of a collar appeared to partially mitigate the adverse mechanical effects of undersizing by improving proximal load transfer. Cite this article: Bone Joint Res 2026;15(11):1354–1363.
papers.first_author_affiliation: First Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, St. Anne’s University Hospital and Faculty of Medicine, Masaryk University, Brno, Czechia

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文用患者特异性有限元模型量化股骨柄尺寸不足对假体周围骨应变的影响，直接对应髋关节假体应力遮挡与初期稳定性方向。
llm.why_not_core: It reports strain intensity and stem von Mises stress but does not quantify micromotion at the bone-implant interface with contact/friction modeling, nor does it report Gruen zone-resolved SED or compare intact versus implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 直接前入路下股骨柄尺寸不足可能损害初期稳定性并改变近端载荷传递。
summary_zh.method: 基于CT构建患者特异性全股骨有限元模型，比较四种柄配置与两种松质骨密度下的应变与应力。
summary_zh.result: 尺寸不足显著提高假体周围骨应变并扩大超载区域，带领设计可部分缓解，柄应力远低于材料极限。
summary_zh.validation: 数值仿真病例，采用Frost力学稳态理论评估应变强度。

summary_en.motivation: Stem undersizing in cementless THA via the direct anterior approach may compromise primary stability and alter proximal femoral load transfer.
summary_en.method: Patient-specific CT-based full-femur FE models compared four AMIStem-P configurations (fit/undersized, collared/non-collared) under two cancellous bone density conditions with a peak walking hip joint force.
summary_en.result: Undersizing markedly elevated periprosthetic trabecular strain and enlarged regions exceeding the 3,000 microstrain overload threshold, while a collar partially mitigated these effects and stem stresses remained well below material limits.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulation case evaluated using Frost's mechanostat theory for strain intensity and von Mises stress in the stem.

papers.title: Research on the optimization of micro-texture parameters of cutting tool surfaces based on finite element method for anti-wear of cutting tools and reduction of chip burr in dry cutting of Ti-6Al-4V
papers.venue: Journal of Mechanical Science and Technology

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Ti-6Al-4V干切削中刀具表面微织构参数优化以减少磨损和切屑毛刺，与增材制造生物医学材料方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses cutting-tool surface micro-texture optimization for machining Ti-6Al-4V, with no LPBF fabrication, no porous implant structure, no stress shielding or stiffness matching, no mechanical/fatigue testing, and no osseointegration or biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 为减少Ti-6Al-4V干切削中的刀具磨损与切屑毛刺。
summary_zh.method: 采用有限元方法优化刀具表面微织构参数。
summary_zh.result: 获得可降低磨损和毛刺的微织构参数组合。
summary_zh.validation: 基于有限元仿真案例验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to mitigate tool wear and chip burr formation during dry cutting of Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Finite element simulation is used to optimize the geometric parameters of surface micro-textures on cutting tools.
summary_en.result: An optimized micro-texture parameter set is identified that reduces tool wear and chip burr.
summary_en.validation: Validation relies on finite element simulation of the cutting scenario.
